item.title: Joint Priorities for an effective WEEE framework revision
item.description: Shared views from across the WEEE value chain on the WEEE revision under the Circular Economy Act The upcoming revision of the Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE) framework and the new Circular Economy Act are an opportunity to make Europe’s circular economy a pillar of its industrial strategy. This paper brings together shared priorities […]

item.title: A circular VAT framework that rewards recycling and restores fair competition
item.description: FEAD, the European Waste Management Association, welcomes the Commission’s initiative to modernise VAT rules to support the transition towards a circular economy. Nevertheless, FEAD deeply regrets the narrow framework proposed and sees this as a missed opportunity to drive real change and to improve competition in the waste management market. The call for evidence does […]

item.title: FEAD feedback to the second workshop on the deposit-return systems for batteries
item.description: FEAD, the European Waste Management Association, welcomes the continued work of Oeko-Institut and Ramboll on the feasibility and potential benefits of deposit-return systems (DRS) for batteries under Article 63 of the Batteries Regulation. FEAD particularly welcomes that the second stakeholder workshop identified fire prevention as the main driver for the discussion on a battery DRS, […]

item.title: FEAD’s feedback on the 2027 Early Warning Report on Waste
item.description: FEAD, the European Waste Management Association, representing the private waste and resource management industry across Europe welcomes the objective of the Early Warning Report (EWR) drawn up by the Commission to assess Member States’ progress towards reaching: (i) the 2030 recycling targets for municipal waste and packaging waste; (ii) the waste food reduction targets for […]

item.title: 48 European organisations call for fair competition through more ambitious EU Trade Defence
item.description: The fight for industrial capacity is reshaping the global landscape. EU upstream and downstream industries face the same challenges: unfair trade practices and persistent overcapacity/oversupply induced by state-driven distortions. This comes at a time when European producers are already confronted, among others, with high energy costs that put the EU’s competitiveness under strain. The EU […]

item.title: FEAD severely questions ‘particular scrutiny’ imposed on exports of metal waste
item.description: A disproportionate rejection for metal waste The ‘particular scrutiny’ imposed by the Commission’s draft list of non-OECD countries authorised to receive non-hazardous waste for recovery regarding ferrous and non-ferrous metal waste, has resulted in rejection of 16 out of 21 of the relevant requests. Only five (EU candidate) countries have been authorised in the draft […]

item.title: FEAD’s key messages on trade restrictions for secondary raw materials
item.description: The forthcoming Circular Economy Act offers an opportunity to strengthen the Single Market for secondary raw materials and place recycling at the heart of Europe’s industrial and competitiveness agenda. FEAD considers that policies affecting trade in secondary raw materials should support this objective by improving market conditions for European recycled materials rather than relying primarily […]

item.title: FEAD contribution to the Call for Evidence on sustainability criteria for plastic recycling technologies under Article 7(9) of the PPWR
item.description: FEAD welcomes the European Commission’s intentions on the sustainability criteria for plastic recycling technologies under Article 7(9) of the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation. This contribution focuses exclusively on the future delegated act establishing those criteria. The sustainability criteria will determine whether recycled plastic produced through a particular recycling pathway may be counted towards the […]

item.title: FEAD contribution to the Call for Evidence on harmonisation of rules for calculating and verifying recycled content in plastic packaging
item.description: FEAD, the European Waste Management Association representing the private waste and resource management industry across Europe, welcomes the upcoming secondary legislation under Article 7 PPWR on the calculation and verification of recycled content. During the development of the SUPD methodology and for chemical recycling, FEAD supported a polymer-only allocation approach, rather than the fuel-use-excluded approach […]

item.title: Joint proposal for an effective mirror clause under Article 7(10) of PPWR
item.description: FEAD, PRE and Recycling Europe recommend introducing under Article 7(10) of the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) a clear Made in Europe preference for plastic recycled content (RC) targets: This document outlines proposals for a robust and effective mirror clause for packaging produced and filled outside the EU, in line with Article 7 of […]

item.title: Joint Statement on draft delegated act on the Green-Listing Initiative for Waste Shipments
item.description: The signatories to this statement represent companies and industries operating across the European recycling ecosystem. Our members are active at different stages of the circular value chain, including the collection, sorting, pre-treatment and processing of end-of-life products and waste, as well as the smelting and refining of metals and other secondary raw materials. Together, our […]

item.title: FEAD’s key messages for the revision of the WEEE Directive under the CEA
item.description: FEAD welcomes the Commission’s intention to modernise the Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Directive within the Circular Economy Act. FEAD also welcomes the intention to turn the WEEE Directive in a Regulation, as the various interpretations of the current framework result in different obligations and conditions in each Member State, contributing to an uneven playing […]

item.title: FEAD’s key demands for competition in waste markets and competitiveness of the sector
item.description: FEAD considers competitive waste markets and a competitive European waste management industry essential conditions for delivering the circular economy. Europe’s ambition to become a global leader in circularity by 2030 will require major private investment in collection, sorting, recycling and recovery capacity. This investment can only take place where operators have fair access to markets […]

item.title: FEAD’s key messages for a solid EPR framework
item.description: FEAD considers that discussions around Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) are too producer-centred[1], focusing primarily on compliance costs and administrative burden. These aspects matter for Europe’s competitiveness, but they are only part of the picture. The rapid expansion of EPR schemes across Europe, often under different governance models, has also raised significant concerns for waste management […]

item.title: Joint Statement: Making PPWR plastic recycled content targets deliver for Europe’s circular economy – A ‘Made in Europe’ approach and robust mirror measures
item.description: The European plastics recycling industry is facing an unprecedented crisis, with numerous plant closures, declining demand, unfair international competition and growing imports of allegedly ‘recyclates’ whose recycled content cannot always be effectively verified. At the same time, the recent Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) sets in its Article 7 mandatory recycled content (RC) targets […]

item.title: The Circular Economy Act must deliver demand-side measures for recycled materials
item.description: FEAD considers insufficient and volatile demand for recycled materials to be the main structural barrier currently holding back Europe’s circular economy. While specific waste streams may face collection, sorting or quality constraints, Europe does not face a general structural shortage of recyclable material. Without predictable demand, additional collection, sorting and recycling capacity cannot become economically […]

item.title: FEAD’s key messages for a streamlined and solid end-of-waste framework
item.description: FEAD’s priority for the Circular Economy Act (CEA) is to make the internal market for waste and recycled materials predictable, integrated, and competition friendly. In relation to the EU’s end-of-waste framework, FEAD highlights three main challenges: FEAD’s key recommendations for the CEA: Urgent streamlining of EU-wide EoW criteria. One of the most persistent regulatory obstacles […]

item.title: Joint Letter: Carbon farming
item.description: Dear M. Holzleitner, dear Ms. Forlin, The application of organic fertilisers and soil improvers, such as compost and digestate, is a cornerstone of carbon farming. When regularly applied to agricultural soils, these products improve soil health, enhance soil organic carbon, and contribute to long-term carbon sequestration, while also supporting nutrient recycling, thereby delivering significant climate, […]

item.title: Joint recommendations for unleashing the circular potential of mineral Construction and Demolition Waste
item.description: Background Construction and Demolition Waste (CDW) is the largest waste stream in the EU, accounting for over a third of all waste generated. As such, it plays a pivotal role in achieving the EU’s circularity and decarbonisation objectives, and particularly the goal of doubling the circular material use rate by 2030, as outlined in the […]

item.title: Enabling EU industrial policy through improved circular material flows: A proportionate green-list route for non-hazardous intra-EU e-waste shipments
item.description: The European e-waste value chain calls on the European Commission to ensure that non-hazardous e-waste destined for recovery within the EU continue to benefit from the green-list procedure under the Waste Shipment Regulation (EU) 2024/1157 beyond 1 January 2027. This is essential to preserve efficient intra-EU circular material flows and support European circular value chains. […]
